title: Actionable Feedback: Improving Model Capabilities from User Edit Data on Clinical Documentation
abstract: arXiv:2611.12904v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being deployed in clinical documentation workflows, where clinicians review and edit their outputs before use. In principle, these clinician edits represent a scalable source of supervision for model training. In practice, not all edits represent actionable feedback: for instance, on data drawn from real-world deployment of an AI clinical documentation product, our review suggests that over 45% of edited outputs contain user-added information that is not directly supported by the inputs to the model. Naively fine-tuning on such edits risks teaching the model to hallucinate. In this paper, we develop a method to address this challenge. Given that real clinician edits on deployed documentation tools are not publicly available, we first develop a taxonomy of clinician-editing behaviors, informed by data from a deployed AI clinical documentation product. translated_title: 可操作的反馈：利用临床文档中用户编辑数据提升模型能力
translated_abstract: 大语言模型越来越多地被部署到临床文档工作流程中，临床医生在使用前会审查并编辑模型的输出。原则上，这些临床医生的编辑代表了模型训练的一个可扩展的监督来源。然而在实践中，并非所有编辑都构成可操作的反馈：例如，通过审查来自AI临床文档产品实际部署的数据，我们发现超过45%的编辑后输出包含用户添加的、模型输入并不直接支持的信息。如果在这种编辑上进行简单微调，会有教会模型产生幻觉的风险。在本文中，我们开发了一种方法来应对这一挑战。鉴于已部署文档工具上的真实临床医生编辑数据并不公开，我们首先基于来自已部署AI临床文档产品的数据，构建了一个临床医生编辑行为的分类体系。然后，我们开发了一种生成……的方法
tldr: 该论文针对临床文档场景中用户编辑数据并非全部可操作的问题（如45%以上编辑包含模型输入不支持的信息），构建了临床医生编辑行为分类体系并开发了区分可操作反馈的方法，以避免微调导致模型产生幻觉。
en_tdlr: This paper builds a taxonomy of clinician-editing behaviors and develops a method to identify actionable feedback in user edits on clinical documentation, enabling model improvement from edit data while avoiding teaching the model to hallucinate.
